transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

What finally pushed me to come in is that I keep getting up during sprint planning or mortgage calls, even when I know I should stay put. I’ll suddenly go get water or decide I need to check something in the other room.
When you get that urge to stand up and leave the meeting, what is usually going through your mind?

It’s like this internal pressure builds up. Even if I’m sitting there looking calm, I feel like I need to move or switch to something else, or at least do something with my hands. If I don’t, I start to feel like I’m crawling out of my skin.
Did you have similar troubles with restlessness or sitting still when you were a child?

Yes. In elementary school, teachers would move my desk or remind me to stay seated because I kept popping up. I also talked before I was called on and rushed through things, even when I understood the work.
Do you find yourself struggling with persistent, excessive worries about everyday matters that you find difficult to control?
I’m not sure I’d call it excessive worry. I do have things on my mind sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed feeling worried all the time or unable to control it.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F41.1 (Generalized anxiety disorder) as patient denies persistent, excessive, uncontrollable worry.
